The Gift of Transplant

By: Mart-Marie Faure | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Organ donations offer a new lease on life for many

Unique Selling Point:
Organ donation and transplantation has given three South African children the gift of a new life. Prior to their transplant operations they each had little hope for the future, but since the procedures their lives have changed dramatically. We take a closer look at at each of the three case studies and how transplant has changed their lives.Two of the kids having recently taken part in the 2017 World Transplant Games in Malaga, Spain.

Summary:
Out of adversity comes success. Kristin & Jacques each received kidneys donated by parents.
Four year old Ntando had a kidney and liver transplant. Without these life-saving procedures life as they know it today would not have been possible. At the age of 11 Kristin contracted chronic kidney disease and within six months she needed a kidney transplant. Her father was a match and donated a kidney. Jacques was born without bladder valves and due to renal disease needed a new kidney by the age of 10. His mother was a match and donated one of her kidneys. Today both Kristin and Jacques lead very active lives. They both participated and excelled at the World Transplant Games in Spain.
Four year old Ntando needed a kidney and a liver transplant.Both his parents were viable matches and willing to donate but a deceased donor was found.

Further information:
Transplants for the treatment of end-stage organ failure are one of the major medical advances of the last 50 years. South African doctors are world leaders in transplantation but the country has one of the lowest percentages of transplantation in the world. This is partially due to cultural and religious beliefs. High blood pressure is very common in the black community eliminating possible donors.
Kidney transplantation is a very cost effective and permanent alternative to dialysis and with a severe shortage in dialysis facilities each transplant helps to allow a new patient on dialysis. Only 8 000 out of 50 000 known South Africans needing dialysis are receiving treatment. Thousands of people are unaware or go undiagnosed.

Children with life-threatening kidney disease often experience difficulty in living normal lives. The Kidney Beanz Trust was established to provide comprehensive support services for these children and families.

Press Release:


The Gift of Transplant
Transplants for the treatment of end-stage organ failure are one of the major medical advances of the last 50 years. In South Africa over
4000 adults and children are waiting for a life-saving organ transplant, but only a few hundred operations are performed every year.
Despite this major hurdle, organ donation and transplantation has giving three South African children the gift of a new life. Carte Blanche
explores this complex and emotional process.

Script:


Gift of Transplant

VISUAL SCRIPT
V/o 14-year old Jacques Boshoff was the youngest member of the South African team that recently took part in the World Transplant Games in Malaga, Spain where he excelled.
Jacques I got 5 medals, one silver and 4 gold. The 4 gold was for tennis, the long jump, the ball throw and the 100m. And 1 silver medal was for table tennis.
V/o Team mate, Kristen Henry, a vibrant 15-year old from Johannesburg managed to top that with 5 gold medals and 2 world records...
Kristen Unfortunately you can only do 5 events...

Derek: Isn't that enough?

No. I would have done all the swimming events if I could and then a few more athletics events.
V/o Both Jacques and Kristen have been living with a donor kidney since 2012.
DEREK ON CAMERA LINK Transplants for the treatment of end-stage organ failure have been one of the major medical advances of the last 50 years. But, the journey is complex and emotional…..
V/o At the age of 11 Kristen developed an acute kidney disease that progressed rapidly into end-stage kidney failure...
Kirsten At the time I wasn't particularly thinking of it because I didn't really understand what was going on. But dialysis was quite a hectic thing – I got really tired and not happy.
V/o With only 20% kidney function she needed a transplant urgently. Kristen’s dad Craig was a viable match and on her 12th birthday she received the ultimate gift of life.
AMANDA The first 48 hours is the most critical and within 24 hours her body had gone into some kind of rejection where her body was saying get this foreign body out of me. It was touch-and-go for the first 24 hours but she pulled through.
V/o But Kristin had an enormously positive approach to her illness and sailed through her transplant and post transplant recovery.
V/o Unlike Kristin, Jacques was born with a bladder and kidney disease and was only 12 days old when he had to undergo the first of many operations.
Slowly over time he went into kidney failure and at the age of 10 needed a transplant.
LINDA I was the first candidate to be tested because we have the same blood group and I didn't want to do anything else – that's the first thing that came up my mind was to donate my kidney. And luckily everything worked out. I was the perfect match.
V/o Children with life threatening kidney disease often experience difficulty in living normal lives.

Paediatric nephrologist Dr Errol Gottlich treats children from all over Africa.

Gottlich The fact of the matter is that is an extremely complicated journey. It affects the child, it affects the parents, the siblings, grandparents. And it certainly is a journey that few families can endure easily.
V/o These young patients at Morningside Clinic are tied to dialysis machines, 3 – four hours daily , three times a week. This is their reality until a suitable donor is found.
Young Kimeya has been on the transplant list for 6 years.
UPSOUND Derek: What's a week in the life of Kemya and Preveshny like?

Don't ask. It isn't easy, it's not easy on any parent I guess and waiting and not knowing is the worst.

Let's not get cheesy here...

She's learn't to be strong...

And very positive as well...
Dr. Errol Gottlich
As a parent living with a child with a life threatening disease is a day by day endurance test. And in fact the only real release from that endurance journey is a transplant. Now unfortunately at the moment there is a lack of donors currently in the South African transplant environment so most individuals who get listed for a kidney transplant will wait anywhere between four to seven years to get a transplant.


V/o Little Ntando, affectionately know as “the one and only” by hospital staff, needed a combined liver and kidney transplant at the age of three.. Thankfully a deceased donor was found.
Mom When you're on the list you just wait for the call. I remember when I was home and I got the call … It's everything that you've been waiting for.
Derek Why is it so difficult to find donors?
Dad It's the religious and traditional beliefs that we have especially in our African cultures. It's very hard and difficult for people to actually give or donate their organs or their family's organs for a good cause. So medical personnel are making money from your grief or your suffering or loss.
V/o After transplant, most kids live a normal live, but a controlled diet , exercise and maintaining a positive attitude is imperative to staying healthy.

Kristin / Amanda


Much healthier
Dr Gottlich We absolutely encourage them as part of their transplant-kidney maintenance r themselves as well and sport and activity is extremely important.


Jaques I have always loved sport – played sport from a young age and my grand father has called me Jacques balletjies.
Gottlich Jacques saw his illness as a speedbump. After his transplant he blossomed as far as his ability is concerned. Jacques has an inherent positive attitude to life
V/o Although Kristin was born with a congenital hand deformity and had to overcome a life-threatening illness, her enormous optimism and determination was rewarded by being voted the Best Female Junior athlete at the Malaga Games.
Amanda
So what does the future hold for Kristin and Jacques?
Jacques
Kristen




PROMO 10” - Derek Link

PROMO 15”
Having a child with a life threatening illness is a difficult journey and something few families can endure……..

Errol Gottlich

PROMO 15” Organ transplantation offers a second chance at life,but the procedure is complex and risky. …

Amanda
